# AET-WO-1500 — FEEDBACK

**Branch:** `wo/aet-1500-mcp` · **Base:** `7b295f8`, merged with `2f13278` (AET-WO-1101, #27/#28) before the push; `Cargo.lock` regenerated by cargo · **Builder:** Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5) as `forge` on Furnace · **Cadence:** build-only; no §7 condition arose.

Entry schema: `finding · where · severity · type · recommendation · decision-needed`.

## What was built

- `aethelgard mcp` (`src/mcp.rs`): `rmcp` **3.7.0** (Apache-2.0, `default-features = false`, features `server` + `transport-io` only) over stdio on a current-thread tokio runtime. `tools()` generates the list from the unbuilt `Cli::command()`; `argv()` is the only builder of a child's vector; a call runs `current_exe()` with stdin `/dev/null`, stdout cap 1 MiB, stderr cap 64 KiB, drains past a cap, and is killed on cancel (`kill_on_drop`). The startup inherited-descriptor check reuses `run::inherited_descriptors` (now `pub(crate)`).
- §1.5a: optional `path` in the refusal envelope (`InvalidIdentifier` only), README row, two tests in `validate_cli.rs`.
- Dependencies: `rmcp` and `tokio` (features `rt macros io-std process signal io-util sync time`; `io-util`, `sync` and `time` are beyond the §1.1 list, used by the drain, `Notify` and a test timeout). Nothing else direct.

### Tool list as printed (`tools/list`)

| tool | description | properties (required) |
|---|---|---|
| `validate` | Validate one JSON Specification read from stdin, or from --file | `file` |
| `check_drc` | KiCad's design rule check on a board (kicad-cli pcb drc) | `board` (yes) |
| `check_erc` | KiCad's electrical rule check on a schematic (kicad-cli sch erc) | `schematic` (yes) |
| `prove` | Prove one Kani harness in a crate and print the verdict | `crate`, `harness` (both) |
| `simulate` | Load a platform in Renode, list the machine it built, and print the verdict | `platform` (yes) |

All strings, `additionalProperties` false.

### What `rmcp` bounds by itself (verified by the adversarial pass)

A line over 16 MiB is dropped with no reply; JSON nesting over serde's 128; it validates no tool arguments (this module does); malformed params get `-32601` not `-32602` in some shapes. It does **not** bound concurrent requests, nor the memory of responses to a client that never reads (one send task per response, no backpressure: 300k `tools/list` grew RSS to 3.5 GB). This module bounds a child's stdout/stderr and nothing about concurrency.

## Findings (adversarial pass: fresh Opus subagent, full, §5)

| # | finding | severity | type | recommendation | decision-needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A `notifications/cancelled` landing while the CLI child is still starting leaves the tool running forever: 17 of 2,500 immediate cancels left `sleep` + `--aethelgard-internal-reaper` under PID 1 (alive 115 s later). Cause: `reaper_main` (`run.rs:416`) samples `parent_id()` at its own start; a CLI SIGKILLed before that sample makes the sample the subreaper, so the later check never fires. Pre-existing in `run.rs`; `mcp` makes it routine (every cancel is a SIGKILL of the CLI) | **high** | bug (security-path) | The CLI passes its own pid in the internal args; reaper and guardian exit at once if `getppid()` already differs. Not done here: `run.rs` reaper protocol is security-path core and outside this WO's fence. Needs its own WO | **yes** |
| 2 | Same race leaks guardians (30 polling forever) and scratch dirs (37 `aethelgard-*` in TMPDIR); 7 more dirs had no guardian (kill between `DirBuilder::create` and the guardian spawn in `Scratch::new`) | medium | bug | Same fix; spawn the guardian first or give it the CLI's pid | yes (with 1) |
| 3 | `SIGHUP`, `SIGQUIT` and `SIGUSR1` are not handled; `SIGKILL` cannot be: CLI child, guardian, reaper and tool survive. Within the letter of §1.4 (TERM and INT) | medium | gap | Add `SIGHUP` (one more arm), and a parent-death signal for the CLI child if a safe setter exists (unverified) | yes |
| 4 | `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` were ignored until `initialize` completed | low | bug | **Fixed**: `serve` is inside the signal `select!`. Tests `sigterm_before_initialize_exits_143` | no |
| 5 | stdin closed before `initialize` exited 70, not 0 | low | bug | **Fixed**: `ConnectionClosed` is a clean end. Test `stdin_closed_before_initialize_exits_0` | no |
| 6 | A client that never reads stdout grows server memory without bound (`rmcp`) | low/medium | risk | Needs a transport wrapper that stops reading while N sends are pending; out of scope. The server is a local stdio child of one client | yes |
| 7 | Concurrent calls are unbounded: 200 at once = 800 processes, 609 fds; under `ulimit -n 200` calls fail cleanly with `isError` and the server lives. README says so | low | risk | A semaphore around `execute`, if a caller needs it | no |
| 8a | Tier-1 cancel/shutdown tests wait for the tool to be running first, so the start-up window of 1 and 2 is unreachable by the suite | low | test gap | Add an immediate-cancel storm test once finding 1 is fixed (it would be flaky red today) | with 1 |
| 8b | With `over.notify_one()` removed, the two cap tests hang instead of failing | low | test | **Fixed**: bounded with `tokio::time::timeout` | no |
| 9 | `rmcp` replies nothing to lone surrogates, invalid UTF-8, duplicate `params`, lines over 16 MiB; wrong-shaped params get `-32601` | info | rmcp | None | no |
| 10a | A legitimate verdict over 1 MiB is `isError`, blamed on a signal | info | wording | **Fixed**: the message names the cap first | no |
| 10b | `structuredContent.verdict` has sorted keys (serde `Map`), so it is not byte-identical to the text | info | note | README now says so; the text is the exact line | no |
| 10c | README said `null` exit code both means killed and "no structuredContent" | info | doc | **Fixed** | no |
| 10d | `rmcp`'s `transport-io` enables `tokio/net`, so the source grep is the only listener guard | info | note | Accepted per §3.6 | no |
| 10e | rmcp 3.7 accepts a stateless `tools/call` without `initialize`; validated identically | info | note | Tests do not exercise it | no |

Not broken (subagent, *ran*): internal first arguments by every tool name and argument name variant (`_ . /`, Unicode look-alikes, `help`, `version`, 500k keys); values with `=`, `--`, newlines, NUL; non-string shapes; result mapping (no non-verdict got past `isError: false`); stdout cleanliness; no stuck drain (only the CLI holds `mcp`'s pipes); no fd leak into children at 200 concurrent calls.

My mutants (one per new guard): `kill_on_drop(false)` fails the cancel and disconnect tests; with `kill_all` also gone the SIGTERM tests fail. A `kill_all` registry on its own **survived**, because dropping the runtime already kills every call, so it was removed (reduction).
